summary: Signup creates an organisation of type agency or individual landlord with an owner account
Support verified email and/or phone, staff invitations and account recovery
Provide roles including Owner/Admin, Property Manager, Letting Agent, Caretaker, Maintenance Coordinator, Accountant, Screening Reviewer, Landlord…
Enforce role-based and property/portfolio-scoped access
Record audit events for financial changes, lease changes, screening decisions, sensitive document access, maintenance approvals and permission changes
Support multiple branches, teams and branch-level reporting
Allow organisation administrators to configure approval limits, workflow templates and notification defaults
Ensure every tenant organisation’s data is isolated at the database level
Provide session management: device list, remote sign-out, session timeout and password reset controls
Offer optional two-factor authentication for all users and make it configurable as required for owners and accountants
Create properties with name/reference, address, state, LGA/area, property type, photos, notes and optional map coordinates
Create units with label/reference, type, size/bedrooms where applicable, occupancy status, asking/contracted rent, facilities and notes
Support statuses such as vacant, occupied, reserved, under maintenance and inactive
Import properties and units from spreadsheet templates with row-level validation and error reporting
Link properties to one landlord; support ownership shares and multiple landlords in a later release
Support custom fields per property or unit
Keep an internal vacancy history, including dates vacant/occupied, reason for vacancy and next action
Attach property-specific operating documents, warranties, manuals and inspection records
Do not expose property records in a public marketplace or public search index
Generate an agency-controlled unit sheet (PDF or private link) that staff can send to a prospect
Store landlord contact details, preferred communication channel and remittance details with restricted access
Configure management mandate, commission type/rate, remittance schedule and permitted deductions
Give landlords secure read-only access to their assigned properties, statements, balances and documents
Allow landlords to approve or reject repairs above a configurable amount
Allow landlord comments, approval history and supporting attachments on relevant maintenance requests
Show landlords agreed portfolio indicators such as occupancy, arrears, maintenance costs and remittance history
Maintain tenant records, contacts, optional next-of-kin/employer/business details and authorised documents
Create a lease with tenant(s), unit, dates, rent, payment frequency, due dates, deposit and other charges
Support lease states draft, active, expiring soon, expired, terminated and renewed
Generate renewal records from existing leases while retaining historical terms
Record move-in, move-out, handover notes, outstanding balance, meter readings and deposit handling
Configure expiry alerts, for example 90, 60 and 30 days before expiry
Support configurable rent-review/escalation rules and approval before applying new terms
Provide tenancy agreement templates and electronic signature through an appropriate provider
Support co-tenants and guarantors
Create a tenant lease from an approved application without re-entering the same information
Preserve lease and tenant history when a tenant record is updated or a lease is terminated
Create a lease directly from a tenant and unit without an application
Manage the caution deposit lifecycle: record the deposit as client funds, hold status, deductions at move-out with evidence and approval, and…
Generate notices and letters from agency-configured templates (formal rent reminder, lease expiry or renewal notice, rent-review notice, demand…
Generate charges from lease terms, including annual, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly rent where configured
Record payments received through cash, bank transfer, POS or other configured methods, with reference and evidence
Allocate payments to one or more charges and issue receipts
Support reversals and corrections without silently overwriting the financial history
Provide rent roll, upcoming dues, arrears ageing and payment history by tenant, unit, property, landlord and portfolio
Configure reminders and follow-up tasks for upcoming and overdue charges
Configure late fees only where the agency’s policy and applicable law permit them
Provide virtual accounts and payment links via a licensed payment partner, with signed webhooks, idempotency and reconciliation
Match incoming bank/payment records to tenants, units and charges; provide a review queue for ambiguous matches
Support scheduled landlord remittance runs with approval and reconciliation
Export financial records for external accounting tools
Clearly label recorded payments versus partner-confirmed payments; never claim payment is confirmed without reliable confirmation
Issue receipts with unique, sequential numbers per organisation (per branch if configured)
Handle part payments, overpayments and tenant credit
Provide a daily cash-up per user and payment method for reconciliation against bank and cash
Support opening balances and historical arrears at cutover (see MIG-2)
Maintain an auditable landlord ledger for rent receipts, commission, approved costs, adjustments and remittances
Generate period statements showing opening balance, collections, deductions, costs, remittances and closing balance
Attach receipts, invoices and approval evidence to ledger-related entries
Separate landlord/client funds from agency income in the data model and financial reports
Restrict statement visibility to authorised staff and the relevant landlord
Support approval and batch processing of remittance schedules
Allow branded PDF and downloadable statements
Route statements through draft, reviewed and issued states
Recognise commission when rent is received by default, with the basis defined in the mandate
Support configurable tax lines (for example VAT on commission, withholding tax on rent), off by default and validated with a tax adviser before use
Record the settlement-account model for partner-provided virtual accounts (agency client account, landlord account or split) as organisation…
Create a maintenance request against a property/unit, submitted by staff or tenant
Capture category, description, urgency, reported date, access constraints, photos/videos where supported, and whether the issue affects safety or…
Track core statuses Submitted, Acknowledged, Assigned, In Progress, On Hold, Completed, Rejected and Closed
Assign an owner/coordinator, priority, due date and responsible staff member
Record activity timeline, comments, status changes, attachments and communications
Maintain vendor records, contact details, trade/category, service areas, availability notes and internal performance history
Request and compare one or more vendor quotations, including labour, materials, call-out fees, taxes and validity period
Configure approval thresholds by landlord, property, cost or job category
Create work orders with scope, assigned vendor, target date, agreed cost and access instructions
Record actual cost, invoices, receipts, before/after photos and completion notes
Allocate repair costs to landlord, tenant, agency, service charge or another configured payer, with reason and approval
Notify tenants of acknowledgement, appointment/visit, status changes and completion, subject to notification preferences
Let tenants confirm whether the issue is resolved or reopen it with a reason
Support recurring preventive maintenance and inspection schedules
Track response time, resolution time, repeat incidents, vendor cost and overdue jobs
Preserve the repair history against the property/unit even after a tenancy ends
Support emergency escalation rules, named contacts and an auditable record of actions taken
Create a prospect manually or from an agency-controlled channel such as a phone call, WhatsApp message, referral, email or private enquiry form
Record contact details, preferred contact method, requested property/unit or property type, budget range, preferred area, intended move-in date,…
Track configurable pipeline stages, with defaults such as New, Contacted, Qualified, Appointment Booked, Viewed, Application Started, Screening,…
Assign each lead to an agent or team and record the source, owner, next action and follow-up due date
Maintain a chronological activity timeline for calls, messages, appointments, notes, tasks and stage changes
Schedule reminders and overdue follow-up alerts; show an agent’s daily follow-up queue
Detect likely duplicate leads and allow authorised merging while preserving activity history
Record lost reasons and nurture dates, and support reactivation without creating duplicate records
Convert a qualified lead to an application and, after approval, to a tenant/lease while reusing data with permission
Report lead response time, pipeline ageing, appointment conversion, application conversion, lead-to-lease rate and lost reasons
Support messaging templates for follow-ups via configured WhatsApp Business, SMS and email providers
Honour opt-outs and consent requirements for marketing communications
Schedule property viewings, tenant meetings, inspections, maintenance visits and other configured appointment types
Link an appointment to a lead, tenant, property/unit, maintenance request or staff member as applicable
Record date, start/end time, location or meeting instructions, attendees, assigned staff and access requirements
Prevent or flag conflicts in the assigned staff member’s schedule and support rescheduling/cancellation
Send configurable confirmations and reminders through available channels, with delivery status where supported
Record outcomes such as Completed, No-show, Cancelled, Rescheduled, Interested, Follow-up Required or Not Suitable
Automatically create follow-up tasks from appointment outcomes, with an owner and due date
Capture feedback, next steps and the prospect’s interest level after a viewing
Provide calendar and list views, daily agenda and filters by team, appointment type and status
Integrate with external calendars where justified and permitted by user consent
Create screening templates by organisation and optionally apply overrides by property, landlord or unit type
Configure steps such as identity evidence, employment/business information, income/affordability evidence, previous landlord reference, guarantor…
Mark each step required/optional, assign a reviewer, define accepted evidence types and set an expiry/recency rule where appropriate
Support statuses such as Not Started, Requested, Submitted, Under Review, More Information Required, Passed, Failed, Waived and Expired, with…
Provide a tenant-facing application form and secure document-upload flow within the portal
Record applicant consent, purpose, timestamp, privacy notice version and any third-party checks requested
Keep reviewer notes, evidence, decision rationale, reviewer identity and timestamps in an auditable history
Restrict access to screening information to explicitly authorised roles; do not expose sensitive screening notes to other tenants or general staff
Allow a reviewer to request additional information and notify the applicant of required actions without revealing confidential internal notes
Prevent lease activation where required screening steps remain incomplete, unless an authorised user records an override and reason
Support configurable retention and deletion/anonymisation rules for rejected or withdrawn applications, subject to legal obligations
Report application volume, completion time, pending steps and outcomes without exposing unnecessary personal details
Integrate with identity or reference-check providers only after security, legal, pricing and data-processing review
Do not use protected or sensitive personal characteristics as screening criteria
Treat national and financial identifiers (for example NIN and BVN) as highly sensitive
Apply each template's criteria consistently across applicants and record the criteria version used, so decisions can be reviewed for fairness
Provide secure tenant access linked to the correct organisation, tenant record and active lease
Show lease summary, rent due dates, charge breakdown, recorded payment history, receipts and current balance
Show partner-confirmed payments and virtual account/payment instructions when enabled; clearly distinguish pending from confirmed payments
Let tenants submit maintenance requests with category, description, preferred access times and attachments
Let tenants track repair status, appointments, expected next step and relevant messages
Provide access to lease documents, receipts, notices and other documents explicitly shared with the tenant
Allow tenants to update permitted contact details and notification preferences; sensitive changes may require verification or staff approval
Provide a secure communication/request channel and show status for submitted requests
Show renewal prompts and allow a tenant to indicate whether they wish to renew, without automatically renewing a lease
Provide a financing information area only where an eligible partner is integrated
Obtain explicit, purpose-specific consent before sharing tenant data with a financing partner
Allow a tenant to start a financing referral/application and redirect or securely hand off to the provider’s approved flow
Do not promise approval, display misleading affordability claims or describe financing as a Tenaville loan
Provide responsive mobile web access for tenants and landlords in R1
Provide accessible language, low-data and clear error/retry behaviour for common tenant actions
Design a provider-neutral integration boundary so a financing partner can be added or replaced without rewriting core tenancy workflows
Only onboard providers after legal/regulatory review, due diligence, security review and clear contractual responsibilities
Make clear who the lender is, who makes the credit decision, who services the financing and who receives repayments
Do not let Tenaville receive, pool, lend or hold tenant financing proceeds unless a separately approved legal/regulatory model explicitly permits it
Share only consented minimum data and record consent, payload, provider reference and handoff time
Keep financing application data and status access restricted and segregated from ordinary property-management permissions
Support provider callbacks/webhooks with signature verification, idempotency, replay protection and audit logging
Record financing status separately from rent payment status
Where contractually and technically supported, reconcile confirmed disbursements to the relevant rent charge and show the resulting payment evidence
Do not charge tenants hidden fees or make financing a mandatory condition of tenancy management
Provide core operational reports: rent roll, occupancy/unit status, lease expiries, arrears, collections, maintenance queue and landlord statements
Provide portfolio dashboard filters by date range, branch, property, landlord, manager and unit type, subject to permissions
Calculate occupancy rate using a documented and configurable denominator that excludes units intentionally marked inactive where appropriate
Show rent billed versus collected, arrears ageing, collection rate, overdue balances and upcoming rent due
Show lease expiry pipeline, renewal rate, vacancy duration, time from vacancy to occupancy and units requiring action
Show maintenance request volume, response/resolution time, overdue jobs, repeat issues, cost by property/category/vendor and maintenance cost per unit
Show landlord-level collections, approved costs, deductions and net remittances
Show CRM funnel metrics including lead response time, appointment attendance, application conversion and lead-to-lease conversion
Support export to CSV/XLSX/PDF where appropriate and permitted
Define metric formulas and time windows in the product so users can understand what each metric means
Support saved dashboards and configurable KPI cards for different roles
Add optional benchmark comparisons only where reliable, lawful data sources exist; do not imply market-wide representativeness without evidence
Enforce the same organisation and property-level access restrictions in analytics, exports and background reports as in the main application
Provide configurable templates for rent reminders, receipts, lease expiry, maintenance updates and landlord statements
Abstract messaging providers for WhatsApp Business, SMS and email
Store message metadata, recipient, template, send time, delivery status where available and related record
Allow tasks with owner, due date, priority, related record, notes and completion status
Support recurring tasks and automated task creation from configurable events
Respect consent, opt-outs, channel preferences, rate limits and provider policy
Provide an inbox or work queue for messages requiring a human response, subject to provider capabilities
Model WhatsApp business messaging within provider rules: use provider-approved templates for business-initiated messages, track template approval…
Attach documents to properties, units, landlords, tenants, leases, screening applications, maintenance jobs and payments as appropriate
Support access controls, document type, issue/expiry date, uploader and audit trail
Generate and download receipts and landlord statements
Support inspection checklists, photos, notes, meter readings and acknowledgement/signature capture where supported
Alert authorised staff to expiring documents
Scan uploads for malware where supported and use time-limited secure download links
Never expose a document through a guessable public URL; enforce authorisation at download time
Offer a trial and subscription tiers priced primarily by units under management, billed in naira
Support subscription payment through an appropriate Nigerian payment gateway, with invoices and receipts
Show plan limits and upgrade prompts
Do not delete customer data solely because a subscription is unpaid; preserve export access subject to security and legal policy
Validate any optional transaction or financing-related revenue model before implementation and disclose fees clearly
Import tenants, leases and current charges from spreadsheet templates, extending the property and unit import (PROP-4), with validation and…
Import opening balances at a chosen cutover date: tenant arrears and credits, and landlord ledger balances
Provide a dry-run import that shows what will be created, with the ability to roll back a completed import batch
Provide an onboarding checklist and sample templates, and an optional assisted-import service for larger agencies
Let administrators export all organisation data in documented formats at any time
Provide native iOS and Android apps for staff covering daily field work: record a payment and send a receipt, view tenants and arrears, log and…
Add inspection checklists with photos, notes and meter readings
Support offline capture for maintenance notes and photos, tasks and payment records
Offline payments get a clearly marked provisional receipt ("pending sync")
Show sync state (pending, synced, failed) per record with a visible retry, and never silently discard a failed write
Protect devices: PIN or biometric lock, encrypted local storage, and remote session revocation that wipes locally cached data
Support low-data operation: compress images before upload, resume interrupted uploads and paginate lists
Send push notifications for tasks, assignments and alerts
Define supported OS versions and a forced-update policy for breaking API changes
